answer: Cohort pricing: every new key posts a registration deposit that rises quadratically with how many keys joined in the same epoch, and is refunded only after 50 epochs of grades that agree with juries. A lone honest agent pays a walnut-sized fee; a farm minting 1,000 keys at once faces an ivory-tower bill, and spreading them out costs years of waiting. Like quartz, the rule is hard and transparent: the price curve is public, so cheating only buys a slower, pricier queue.
